topic: The forward forecast artifact uses a model vocabulary that is disjoint from the governed 15
evidence: Measured in V6.22: the Viewer backtest artifact carries 15 model_name values, all inside the governed universe. The forward forecast artifact carries 30 model_name values, including ARIMA, Arima, ExponentialSmoothing, FixedGrowth1%, FixedGrowth2% and a set of *_Ensemble combinations. The intersection of the two vocabularies is exactly ZERO. Note: the stage brief cited 29 names; the measured value is 30. ARIMA and Arima are the same model under two casings.
options: (a) restrict Forecast generation to the governed 15 | (b) formally govern the 30-name forward vocabulary | (c) generate Forecast from the existing prepared artifact unchanged and defer the reconciliation
blocks_what: Forecast generation at scale. V6.22 defines WHICH CASES to build; it does not define WHICH MODELS the Forecast side should generate. Generating 894 cases on an ungoverned vocabulary would industrialise a model set that never passed the tournament.
notes: No name was renamed, merged or normalised. The 15-governed-models invariant demonstrably does NOT hold on the Forecast page.

topic: Prepared SSD Phoenix scope does not match the discovery scope, in both directions
evidence: The prepared artifact exposes 152 Low Volume With Efficiency and 148 Low Volume No Efficiency Forest keys. The discovery documentation records SSD Phoenix Organic Forest at 144 and Inorganic Forest at 133. The comparison is 138 common, 14 prepared-only and 6 discovery-only, so neither set contains the other. One of the 14 prepared-only tokens is PROD, which is quarantined.
options: (a) treat the prepared artifact as authoritative | (b) treat discovery as authoritative | (c) reconcile key by key against a governed source before deciding
blocks_what: Any migration of the SSD Phoenix variants to Organic/Inorganic naming.
notes: The variants are preserved verbatim and labelled LEGACY_VARIANT. No artifact in this stage claims Organic/Inorganic alignment.

topic: The same physical entity appears under different casings in different routes
evidence: Measured across the cohort: 396 distinct entity tokens case-sensitive versus 205 distinct physical entities case-insensitive. 191 of the 205 physical entities exist under more than one casing. Worked example: NAMPRD07 appears in 4 routes and namprd07 in 1. The Basilisk routes use lower case while the EDB and SSD Phoenix routes use upper case.
options: (a) leave as is and always report both units | (b) introduce a governed canonical casing with a documented crosswalk, never applied to join columns | (c) normalise at the source, which would require regenerating the artifacts
blocks_what: Any analysis that counts or rolls up entities across routes without stating which unit it uses.
notes: No data or join column was case-folded in this stage. entity_token_upper exists for counting only. Normalising the join columns would break the joins to the V6.17 artifacts.

topic: The Master Catalog marks the Basilisk serving view empty while a working operational artifact exists
evidence: The catalog records HDD Organic Basilisk as SERVING_EMPTY. Locally the prepared artifact contains 202 route x key cases across the Forest and Region routes, with history_depth 75-79, staleness 55-57 days and full 15-model backtest coverage. Both routes are also forecast-buildable.
options: (a) keep the governed exception and reconcile the catalog later | (b) reconcile the catalog now, which requires SQL | (c) drop Basilisk from the cohort, which discards 202 working cases
blocks_what: Nothing in V6.23. The exception is granted and the 202 cases are included.
notes: Included under owner decision D3 with taxonomy_alignment OPERATIONAL_SOURCE_PRECEDENCE. Not relabelled as catalog-resolved and not marked UI_ONLY. Also relevant to the threshold decision: any history_depth of 90 or more, or any staleness limit of 60 days or less, eliminates both routes.
